audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings put Eternal Hunger's healing threshold on AMBESSA's health instead of Warwick's: 'his passive heals him on every basic', 'the lower your HP the more his Q heals', 'his passive heals him harder the lower he drops you', 'his passive heals off your low HP', 'his passive lifesteals on every hit', 'a passive that heals to full off your low bars'.
audit.why: Eternal Hunger is gated on WARWICK's own health, not the target's. Above 50% of his health his basic attacks are bonus magic damage and heal him nothing at all; below 50% they heal for that amount, and below 25% the healing triples. The entry has the mechanic pointed the wrong way, and the resulting advice is the opposite of correct twice over. It tells the player to fear a full-health Warwick's auto sustain, which does not exist — levels 1-3 are the window where his attacks are pure damage — and it fails to warn about the real trap, which is taking him below half and then failing to finish, where his healing doubles and then triples against you.
audit.corrected: Eternal Hunger (P): bonus magic damage on his attacks, and healing only once HE is under 50% health — tripled under 25%. A full-health Warwick sustains nothing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json — P Eternal Hunger: 'If Warwick is below 50% health, he heals the same amount. If Warwick is below 25% health, this healing triples.'

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings call Infinite Duress a 'point-and-click channeled suppress' (spikes[2].text, mid, whys[4]).
audit.why: It is a directional LEAP that suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5 seconds — it can miss, and another body in the path eats it. Calling it point-and-click tells the Ambessa player that the ability is unavoidable and that the only counterplay is to never be at level 6 with her R down, when in fact a minion between the two of them, or one dash held back for the leap, beats it outright. The leap distance also scales with his bonus move speed, which chains straight into Blood Hunt below.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress (R), 110/90/70: a directional leap, distance scaling with his bonus move speed, that suppresses the FIRST champion it collides with for 1.5s. Body-block it or dash it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json — R Infinite Duress: 'Warwick leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed), suppressing the first champion he collides with for 1.5 seconds', cd 110/90/70

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: It is 15s at rank 1 and it is the single ability that most directly beats Ambessa's damage pattern: 2.5 seconds of flat damage reduction, ending in — or re-activated early as — a 1-second fear on everyone nearby. Ambessa's damage arrives as one compressed Q-into-empowered-auto burst, so a Howl that covers those 2.5 seconds converts her whole rotation into chip, and the fear on the back end interrupts the dash chain she needs to leave with. The entry's central instruction, 'commit your full all-in at Eclipse', walks straight into it. Baiting Primal Howl before committing is the missing step.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl (E), 15/14/13/12/11: 2.5s of damage reduction, then a 1s fear. Bait it out before you spend the combo.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json — E Primal Howl: 'gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second', cd 15/14/13/12/11

audit.whatIsWrong: Blood Hunt is treated as a permanent chase tool — 'Blood Hunt's move speed lets him walk through it', 'Pop Blood Hunt to chase you down' — and Jaws of the Beast's damage is called low-HP scaling.
audit.why: Blood Hunt only senses and buffs against enemies already below 50% health, tripling below 25%, and it is an 80-second cooldown at rank 1. That makes it conditional and countable rather than constant, and it gives Ambessa a live target to play toward: stay above half and it never switches on, which also keeps his R leap at its base distance since the leap scales with bonus move speed. Jaws of the Beast, meanwhile, deals damage based on the target's MAXIMUM health and heals for damage dealt on an 8-second cooldown — so it is health stacking, not low health, that feeds it, and armour is the wrong item answer.
audit.corrected: Blood Hunt (W), 80s at rank 1: only activates against targets under 50% health, triples under 25%. Jaws of the Beast (Q), 8s: max-health damage that heals him for what it deals.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json — W Blood Hunt cd 80/70/60/50/40, Q Jaws of the Beast 'damage based on their maximum health and healing for damage dealt', cd 8/7.5/7/6.5/6

audit.whatIsWrong: diff is EVEN at 6/10 against a 39.81% win rate over 309 games — the worst matchup in Ambessa's top-lane table by a wide margin.
audit.why: I have not changed it, because diff and diffRating are mirrored pairs and the Warwick page has not been audited yet, so a unilateral move to HARD would just be overwritten. But the gap is too large to leave unflagged: an EVEN badge on a sub-40% matchup tells the player to take a fight the data says they lose. The kit backs the data — a directional suppress, an 8s max-health heal, damage reduction into a fear, and healing that triples when he is low all point one way.
audit.corrected: Should very likely read HARD, with diffRating and the Warwick page's mirror value moved together. Needs a human decision — see questionsForUser.

edits.before: Warwick's passive heals him on every basic and his Q heals more the lower your HP gets, so every short trade you win he licks back before you can re-engage — and your level 1 is one ability and energy-gated, so you concede the opener. Your E spin and its near-total slow is your one early tool to pin him in an empowered-auto window, but Blood Hunt's move speed lets him walk through it, so save E for when you actually commit, not to chip.

Last-hit at the outer edge of Cunning Sweep where it doubles, and don't throw a Q just to poke; Jaws of the Beast is back every 8s and heals him for what it deals. Your E spin and its near-total slow is your one early pin, and Blood Hunt only switches on once you are under half, so keeping your own bar high keeps him slow.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your weakest window and his sustain is fully online — do not force extended fights here, because his passive and Q out-heal your combo damage and you have no kill threat yet. At 6 his R is the problem: it's a point-and-click channeled suppress that interrupts your dash-into-empowered-auto chains and answers your own R, so if you blink behind and suppress, he simply R's back, breaks your animation, and locks you while his passive heals off your low HP. Bait his R or fight only when it's down — never trade your suppress into his.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your weakest window — your cooldowns are longest and an 8s Jaws of the Beast refunds him off your max health, so don't force extended fights you cannot finish. At 6 his R is the problem, but not the way it is usually described: Infinite Duress is a directional leap that suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s, so a minion in the path eats it and a held dash beats it. The leap also scales with his bonus move speed — stay above 50% health, Blood Hunt never triggers, and his R stays short. Bait Primal Howl before you commit.

edits.before: Your one real favor window is your first item: Eclipse plus a Q rank lets Cunning Sweep → Sundering Slam plus an empowered auto chunk him faster than his Q and passive can recover, so all-in there or never. notes: THE PASSIVE WAS POINTED THE WRONG WAY in six separate strings — Eternal Hunger keys off Warwick's own health, not the target's — and that single inversion was driving the whole page's advice. Worth checking whether other Warwick matchups across the site carry the same reversal, since it reads like one bad source sentence copied outward.
